domain_description.quote: Meaning is therefore always orientation by the true, by what is and by what is experienced as reality. Meaning is unconditionally realistic. The person living meaningfully will face and grasp the facts.
domain_description.citation_apa: Längle, A. (1992). What Are We Looking for When We Search for Meaning? Ultimate Reality and Meaning, 15(4), 306–314, p. 312. https://doi.org/10.3138/uram.15.4.306

definition.quote: Man sees that the world is continually effecting him. Acting, he realises that he in turn has an effect on the world. In this way he experiences his special relation with the world, in which he stands. This 'being-in-the-world' (Heidegger) is the fundamental state man finds himself in, his basic ontological experience.

existential_needs.name: Orientation to Facts / Ground to Hold

support.quote: Meaning is unconditionally realistic. The person living meaningfully will face and grasp the facts. He needs their ground to hold and support him, in order to act and receive effects.

Not even success serves as protection. Just at the point where work loses its quality of necessity for life, a vacuum of orientation is formed and causes the afflicted person to indeed have everything he can live from, but nothing more he can live for.

inclusion_criteria.text: References to grasping facts, reality testing, or needing ground/support from facts.

support.quote: Meaning is therefore always orientation by the true, by what is and by what is experienced as reality... will face and grasp the facts.

indicators.text: Mentions of being affected by the world and affecting it; descriptions of fundamental state as 'being-in-the-world'.

support.quote: Man sees that the world is continually effecting him. Acting, he realises that he in turn has an effect on the world... This 'being-in-the-world'... is the fundamental state man finds himself in.

example_quotes.quote: The seeker of meaning first looks for reality, searches for facts and conditions.

source_trace.source_title: What Are We Looking for When We Search for Meaning?
source_trace.direct_quote: Man sees that the world is continually effecting him... This 'being-in-the-world'... Meaning is unconditionally realistic... face and grasp the facts.

definition.quote: In the theory of motivation its correlate is the will to existence, with its yes or no to the world, its will to unfold or refuse action.

inclusion_criteria.text: Statements about wanting to exist, to unfold, or refusing action in relation to the world.

codes.name: Conditions for Being: Protection, Space, Support

definition.quote: This demands three things: protection, space and support.
definition.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

support.quote: Do I enjoy protection, acceptance, do I feel at home somewhere?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

support.quote: Do I have enough space for being there?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

support.quote: Where do I find support in my life?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

support.quote: Each fundamental motivation has four types of coping reactions: the basic reaction type – here this would be avoidance or flight;
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

support.quote: the paradoxical reaction type or activism – here this would be overactivity like fighting bacteria by compulsive washing;
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

support.quote: the third type of coping reaction is a specific aggression... here it would be a destructive aggression such as hate;
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

support.quote: the last type of coping reaction is a reflex of freezing, of death imitation with paralysis – here denial or pretending to be non-existent.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

inclusion_criteria.text: Mentions of needing or lacking protection, space, or support to 'be'.

support.quote: This demands three things: protection, space and support.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

indicators.text: References to fundamental trust in world/self arising from secured protection, space, support.

support.quote: But if I do have these three things, I will be able to feel trust in the world and confidence in myself... The sum of these experiences of trust is the fundamental trust...
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 5).

source_trace.direct_quote: I am - can I be?... This demands three things: protection, space and support... fundamental trust.
source_trace.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

definition.quote: My active part in this fundamental condition of being here is to accept the positive and endure the negative.
definition.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 31).

support.quote: If this is not the case, psychodynamic forces take over the guidance in the form of coping reactions, which aim secure life.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 31).

inclusion_criteria.text: Mentions of accepting conditions, occupying space, relying on support, trusting protection; enduring the difficult/unalterable.

support.quote: To accept means to be ready to occupy the space, to rely on the support and to trust the protection... To endure means to have the strength to persist... and to ‘support’ what cannot be changed.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 31).

indicators.text: Consequences of unmet conditions: restlessness, insecurity, fear.

support.quote: If these conditions of existence are not met, the result will be restlessness, insecurity and fear.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 31).

source_trace.source_title: The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations...
source_trace.direct_quote: My active part... is to accept the positive and endure the negative... restlessness, insecurity and fear.
source_trace.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36.

additional_descriptions.quote: The first condition arises from the simple fact that I am here at all, that I am in the world... I am - can I be? Can I claim my place in this world under the conditions and with the possibilities I have?
additional_descriptions.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 4–5).

additional_descriptions.quote: But I am here... I may ask myself: Can I claim my place in this world under the conditions and with the possibilities I have? A positive answer... demands three things: Protection, space and support.
additional_descriptions.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 31).

domain_description.quote: So man experiences his unfolding of action in a network structure of the world's relations... This is not only a factual experience, however, but fundamentally an experience of value. He not only knows that he is, but that in itself it is also good to be.

codes.name: Will to Value & Conscience as Organ of Meaning

definition.quote: Man continually faces the axiological question of meaning: 'What is good about it?', 'What is it good for?'... conscience which Frankl therefore also calls the 'organ to find meaning' (Sinn-Organ).

support.quote: At the same time, search for meaning includes the desire for the attractive, the desire for dealing with the valuable which man wants to give as much as to receive.
We observe that the question explicitly forces itself upon man during phases when meaning is lost... Here primarily losses of value should be mentioned.

inclusion_criteria.text: Mentions of evaluating good/harmful, beneficial/obstructive; explicit reference to conscience guiding value sense.

support.quote: With regard to that, things are more or less good, beneficial or harmful, useful or obstructive... conscience... the 'organ to find meaning'.

indicators.text: Questions like 'What is good about it?' or 'What is it good for?'

support.quote: Man continually faces the axiological question of meaning: 'What is good about it?', 'What is it good for?'

source_trace.source_title: What Are We Looking for When We Search for Meaning?
source_trace.direct_quote: Losses of value... Man continually faces the axiological question... desire for the attractive... give as much as to receive.

codes.name: Conditions for Loving Life: Relationship, Time, Closeness

definition.quote: In order to seize my life, to love it, I need three things: relationship, time and closeness.
definition.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

support.quote: Do I have relationships, in which I feel closeness, for which I spend time and in which I experience community?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

support.quote: Do I take time for valuable things, worthy to spend my time for?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

support.quote: Can I feel close and maintain closeness to things, plants, animals and people? Can I admit the closeness of someone else?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

support.quote: The basic coping reaction on this level is regression.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

support.quote: The activism here is overprotection or achievement, typical forms of combating evil;
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

support.quote: the typical aggression is fury, rage which does not lead to destruction, but wants to agitate the other person with the impulse to obtain or to improve the relationship.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

support.quote: Resignation reaction of feigned death paralyzed half-way.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

support.quote: I need three things: relationship, time and closeness.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

codes.name: Active Participation: Turning Toward & Consenting to Feelings

definition.quote: I seize life (carpe diem), engage in it, when I turn toward other people... When I move towards it, get close... If life is to make me move freely, my consent to being touched (to my feelings) is a prerequisite.
definition.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 32).

coping_reactions.type: Progression of Lack → Longing → Coldness → Depression

support.quote: If relationships, closeness and time are lacking, longing will arise, then coldness and finally depression.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 32).

inclusion_criteria.text: Mentions of turning toward people/things/self; consenting to feelings as prerequisite to live freely.

support.quote: I seize life... when I turn toward other people... If life is to make me move freely, my consent to being touched... is a prerequisite.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 32).

indicators.text: Experience of harmony with world/self and depth of life when conditions met.

support.quote: If these three conditions are fulfilled, I can experience myself as being in harmony with the world and with myself, and I can sense the depth of life.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 32).

source_trace.source_title: The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations...

source_trace.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36.

additional_descriptions.quote: Therefore I am confronted with the fundamental question of life: I am alive – do I like this fact? Is it good to be there?
additional_descriptions.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 6).

additional_descriptions.quote: Therefore I am confronted with the fundamental question of life: I am alive – but do I like this fact? Is it good to be here?
additional_descriptions.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 32).

domain_description.quote: He experiences consequences in: a) present and future effects on life by what has been done (responsibility), b) the right to live amidst all of life's relations, especially the social structure (justification).

definition.quote: He experiences things not only as ontologically given and not only as an axiological incentive but also knows the world as existentially challenging... He finds himself up against the question: 'What do I do as a free, creative and responsible person in the middle of this world?'

existential_needs.name: Need for Relations (to self and others)

support.quote: Finally, the need for relations is alive in meaning, for relating to oneself (responsibility) as well as to others, which enables the justification of existence.
Besides loss of value and lack of orientation in work, lack of relations is another phenomenon causing the existential vacuum.

inclusion_criteria.text: References to responsibility, justification, or being challenged to decide what to do amid relations.

support.quote: The things that are there continually face him as the deciding person with the question: 'What are you doing to do with it?'... responsibility and justification.

indicators.text: Mentions of social structure, right to live among relations, justification of existence.

support.quote: The right to live amidst all of life's relations, especially the social structure (justification).

source_trace.source_title: What Are We Looking for When We Search for Meaning?
source_trace.direct_quote: Lack of relations... existentially challenging... 'What do I do as a free, creative and responsible person...'?

codes.name: Conditions for Being Oneself: Attention, Justice, Appreciation

definition.quote: In order to succeed here, it is necessary to have experienced three things: attention, justice and appreciation.
definition.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

support.quote: By whom am I seen? Who considers my uniqueness and respects my boundaries?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

support.quote: Do people justice to me?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

support.quote: For what am I appreciated – for what can I appreciate myself?
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

support.quote: The coping reactions of this motivation are: distancing oneself as the basic reaction,
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

support.quote: stubborn insistence and leading a functional life as form of activism.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

support.quote: The typical aggressive reaction consists in indignation, annoyance – anger, reproach.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

support.quote: The freezing type of reaction at this level are dissociation of the bodily integrity, dividing and splitting of emotion and cognition.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

inclusion_criteria.text: Mentions of attention, justice, or appreciation as basis for identity/authenticity.

support.quote: necessary to have experienced three things: attention, justice and appreciation.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

support.quote: If these experiences are missing, solitude will be the result, hysteria as well as a need to hide behind the shame.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 7).

codes.name: Active Participation: Encounter & Regret; Saying Yes to Myself

definition.quote: I also have to say “yes to myself”. This requires my active participation: To look at other people, to encounter them and, at the same time, to delineate myself and to stand by my own, and to refuse whatever does not correspond to myself. Encounter and regret are the two means by which we can live our authenticity...
definition.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 33).

coping_reactions.type: Loneliness, Hysteria, Shame when Missing Attention/Justice/Appreciation

support.quote: If these experiences are missing, loneliness will be the result, hysteria (histrionic disorders) as well as a need to hide behind shame.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 33).

inclusion_criteria.text: Mentions of saying yes to oneself, delineation, refusal of the incongruent; encounter and regret to live authenticity.

support.quote: I also have to say “yes to myself”... delineate myself... refuse whatever does not correspond to myself. Encounter and regret are the two means...
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 33).

indicators.text: Outcomes when present: finding authenticity, relief, self-respect.

support.quote: If... I experience these qualities, I will find myself, find my authenticity, my relief and my self-respect.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2003). The Art of Involving the Person – Fundamental Existential Motivations as the Structure of the Motivational Process. European Psychotherapy, 4(1), 25–36. (p. 33).

domain_description.quote: The existential question of meaning leads up to the decision about the best possibility in a situation, which might also stand as a definition for existential meaning.

definition.quote: Knowing at this point what he can do, what he wants to do and what he may do, he finally realises what he should do - ready to engage himself thanks to his will to act.

support.quote: In the face of death as absolute finis to our future and boundary to our possibilities, we are under the imperative of utilizing our lifetimes to the utmost, not letting the singular opportunities... pass by unused.

inclusion_criteria.text: Statements about deciding the best possibility, commitment, or acting on opportunities under time's finitude.

support.quote: The existential question of meaning leads up to the decision about the best possibility in a situation... we are under the imperative of utilizing our lifetimes to the utmost.

indicators.text: Language of 'should do', 'ready to engage', 'utilizing lifetime', 'opportunities'.

support.quote: He... finally realises what he should do - ready to engage himself... 'utilizing our lifetimes to the utmost'.

codes.name: Phenomenological Openness & Definition of Existential Meaning

definition.quote: This attitude of openness represents the existential access to meaning in life: that dealing with the questions put before me in each situation... 'What does this hour want from me, how shall I respond?'
definition.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 8–9).

inclusion_criteria.text: Mentions of deciding for the most valuable realistic possibility here-and-now.

support.quote: We define meaning as “the most valuable, realistic possibility of the given situation, for which I feel I should decide myself”.
support.citation_apa: Längle, A. (2002). Existential fundamental motivation. In Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Pub Inc. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf (p. 9).

indicators.text: Language of correspondence with the situation; checking good for others/self/future/environment.
